decisions.reason: The same-message introduction already defines logging after each Reel and recording the Instagram Reel link; the publication-format change requires no additional state change.
Publishing as an Instagram Reel does not alter the independently specified one-per-day cadence or 6 PM to 9 PM posting window.
The Reel format does not change the dedicated account's creation, presentation, profile, or audience-routing requirements.
Tracking every published clip and its performance metrics remains valid regardless of the newly specified Instagram Reel format.
The same source already introduces the caption, hashtags, and account-tag placement; specifying Reel as the publication format does not modify those metadata rules.
The publication format for approved clips does not change the deferred monthly approved-clip quota.
Publishing approved clips as Reels does not change who approves clips, which clips count, or the correction and approval rules.
Instagram Reels is already among the target channels, and the Instagram-specific publishing instruction does not remove YouTube Shorts or TikTok from the broader channel-targeting requirement.

The Reel-format decision does not revise the earlier five-clip production deliverable; the instruction to publish three approved clips can describe a publishable subset rather than a changed production count.
The completed initial trial batch is independent of the later publication format for approved production clips.
Publishing a clip as an Instagram Reel does not change its background-music requirement, volume rule, or music-selection rule.
The Instagram Reel format does not modify the established 45-to-60-second duration requirement.
